clue.text: Excellent meeting comprises conservationists lacking community instincts

indicators.note: comprises tells us the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: excellent is A1, written here as AI
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage and conservation body
a social is a friendly gathering or meeting

explanation.surface: A great get-together turns out to be full of nature lovers who shun company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent' is A1, which crosswords often write with the digit as the letter I; 'comprises' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone antisocial avoids or disregards the company and conventions of other people.

clue.text: It may afflict half of us in later life

definitions.text: It may afflict half of us in later life

indicators.note: in places the half-word inside the other piece

parts.note: later life is old age, AGE

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word us leaves just its first letter

explanation.surface: A warning that one in two of us will suffer something as we grow old.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: U (half of 'us') goes in AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague, a malarial fever with shivering fits, is an affliction that may strike.

clue.text: Small duck taking drink on lake

parts.note: tea is a drink
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A little bird sips at the water's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a species of small freshwater dabbling duck.

clue.text: Whose characters support secrecy and unexpectedly excel?

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath the other one

parts.note: stealth is secrecy, acting unseen

indicators.note: unexpectedly tells us the letters of whose come out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whose letters back up a covert agent and then shine without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whose characters' means the letters of WHOSE, which 'unexpectedly' rearranges to ESHOW; 'support' puts that under STEALTH in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal the show is an idiom for outshining everyone else present.

clue.text: Member gets cold at top of ascent

indicators.note: in a down answer, at top of puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: An arm or leg turns chilly on a mountain ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an upward journey, the same as an ascent.

clue.text: Accommodation suitable for housing male painters

indicators.note: housing means the first piece contains the second

parts.note: apt means suitable
men of art, read as art men

explanation.surface: Lodgings that are fit to take in a crew of men who paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'male painters' is read loosely as ART MEN; 'housing' puts them inside APT.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms one lives in.

clue.text: Goddess who lives on an island

parts.note: is, in the sense of exists or lives
Is is an abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A deity said to dwell on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the chief mother deity of ancient Egyptian religion.

clue.text: Ultimately it's very little, the cunning of a lover

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of it's

parts.note: wee is Scottish for very small
art can mean cunning or artfulness

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that a lover's craftiness amounts to almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a beloved partner, someone loved.

clue.text: Sweet old man with a young 7?

definitions.text: Sweet old man with a young 7?

parts.note: sugar is a sweet substance
old man is slang for father, daddy

explanation.surface: An elderly gentleman with a much younger beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 refers to the answer at 7-down, a young lover; the whole clue defines and the first part also builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar daddy is a rich older man who lavishes gifts on a much younger partner.

clue.text: Rumanian church working against US interests

indicators.note: working signals the letters are being worked into a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A Romanian churchman acts against America.
explanation.definitionFit: Un-American describes conduct seen as contrary to the values or interests of the United States.

clue.text: Hill of South Africa, a composer of note

explanation.surface: A South African hill shares its name with a celebrated composer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Afrikaans a berg is a mountain or hill; Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Shrewd bargaining for the Arabs?

explanation.surface: Hard-nosed haggling, as practised by Arabian dealers.
explanation.walkthrough: Arabs here are the horse breed, so dealing in Arabs is literally trading horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-trading is hard, canny negotiation; literally it is buying and selling steeds such as Arab thoroughbreds.

clue.text: Hurried traveller, a bouncer from Harlem…

explanation.surface: A busy tourist and a doorman from New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The Harlem Globetrotters are a famous US exhibition basketball team; the bouncer is a ball-bouncing player, not a doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: A globetrotter travels widely and fast; the Harlem team members dribble basketballs.

clue.text: Booty left in a wet blanket

parts.note: the spoils are plunder or booty
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Plunder is abandoned inside a soggy bedcover.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport ruins others' fun, exactly what a killjoy or wet blanket does.

clue.text: State of a vessel permanently at Gravesend?

parts.note: SS is steamship, a vessel
ever means always or permanently
read as grave's end, the final letter of grave

explanation.surface: A question about a ship moored for good at the Kent port of Gravesend.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravesend is a town on the Thames in Kent; split as grave's end it gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is to declare or affirm solemnly, as one does in stating something.

clue.text: …and has to step out very quickly

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone must step out sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the clue to 12-across for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-haste means with great speed, as fast as the old mail riders.

clue.text: His way to speak is with hesitation

definitions.text: His way to speak is with hesitation
definitions.note: describes a man whose speech catches and repeats sounds, a halting talker

parts.note: a stutter is a halting manner of speech
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A man who speaks only after a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and also builds it, with 'is with' joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: One who stammers speaks haltingly, repeating sounds involuntarily.

clue.text: Novel a bishop returned to the queen

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's novel

indicators.note: returned means the two small pieces are read backwards

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A book and a churchman are sent back to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen of Sheba is the biblical monarch who visited Solomon.

clue.text: It's included a type measurement for news reports

indicators.note: included means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: taken as the letters ITS
an em is a printer's unit of type width

explanation.surface: A printer's measure finds its way into the newspaper pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Items are individual pieces or stories in a news bulletin or newspaper.

clue.text: Turned out badly, not having formal education

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Things went wrong because nobody had been schooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Untutored means without teaching or schooling.

clue.text: Hurry up and put an end to the gossip

definitions.text: put an end to the gossip

explanation.surface: Urging speed and an end to idle chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas is chatter, and to step on something is to squash it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping on the gas means accelerating a car; literally it is crushing idle talk.

clue.text: In old age, a name given to an antelope

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces go inside the old-age word

parts.note: eld is an archaic word for old age

explanation.surface: An animal is given a name in its later years.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: Let slip some gun dogs

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hunter lets a few retrievers off the leash.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or lead is to loosen it, releasing what it held.

clue.text: Silent type many beat severely

parts.note: C is a hundred in Roman numerals, a large number
lam means to thrash

explanation.surface: A quiet person is badly beaten by a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To clam up is to go quiet, so a clam is a taciturn person.

clue.text: The wine isn't started, though it's all right

indicators.note: isn't started means the wine's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine

explanation.surface: The bottle hasn't been opened, though all is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay is a casual way to say acceptable or fine.

clue.text: Unreasonable share in rail disruption

indicators.note: in puts the share inside the rearranged letters
disruption tells us the letters of rail are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: Dividing up the shares during a train strike is illogical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail disruption' tempts as a railway strike, but rail is only the fodder; 'disruption' scrambles it and 'in' places the share inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrational means not guided by reason or logic.

clue.text: Precious box, perhaps, for an imperfect speaker?

indicators.note: someone who cannot form the sounds properly, like a small child, might say TV this way

parts.note: the box is slang for television, TV

explanation.surface: A dainty container for someone with a lisp.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is British slang for the television; a child mispronouncing TV produces the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious and twee both describe something affectedly dainty or sweet.

clue.text: Seek opportunity to free imprisoned Laird of Bucklaw

indicators.note: imprisoned means the second piece is shut inside the first

parts.note: to beg is to seek or ask for
rid means to free
room, as in room for improvement, means scope or opportunity

explanation.surface: A plea to release a captive Scottish lord.
explanation.walkthrough: The Laird of Bucklaw is the man Lucy Ashton marries in Scott's The Bride of Lammermoor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scott's novel the Laird of Bucklaw is the bride's husband on the wedding day.
